text.p: Big screen cinema operator Cinema Plus Ltd said it plans to list on the Australian Stock Exchange on October 10 after a successful public share offer.
The company said the offer of 31 million shares at A$1.00 each was fully subscribed, with many applications scaled back to meet demand for the stock.

The company, which is developing giant screen cinemas in Australia and New Zealand, has 75 million shares on issue with 58.7 percent of the stock held by existing shareholders including executive vice-chairman Gary Blom and a subsidiary of Macquarie Bank Ltd.
The issue was underwritten by Prudential-Bache Securities.
Cinema Plus has the exclusive contract for development of large format IMAX cinemas in Australia and New Zealand.
The company has forecast a net profit of A$2.7 million for the year to June 1997 on sales of A$13.6 million.
The net profit is forecast to rise to A$6.4 million on sales of A$27.3 million in 1997/98.
